The user says: "Please automate the whole process. Just by connecting the phone via USB or the option you tell me, install everything."

Context: The user was asked for GitHub token/repo via requestEnvs, but instead of providing credentials, they replied with this message wanting full automation. No GITHUB_TOKEN env values were provided (the tool returned "awaiting_user_input" and now user just typed a message without credentials).

Key reality check:
1. Without GitHub credentials, I cannot push to GitHub or run CI. The user didn't provide the token.
2. The first installation on Windows fundamentally requires running AcousticalEstudioSetup.exe once on the PC — that cannot be avoided without the installer existing. There's a chicken-and-egg: the resident Windows program that auto-installs/updates doesn't exist on the PC until it's installed once.

Can I "automate everything" including first install? Options:

A) First-time install via ADB only: If the PC had adb... but the PC doesn't have adb or our app. Actually, could the phone push the installer to the PC and execute it via ADB? ADB can't execute arbitrary programs on Windows host. No.

B) What CAN be automated: after one-time install, everything is automatic (autostart, USB watchdog, auto-update). The user's request "solo con conectar el móvil por USB instale todo" — the update flow already does that. The missing piece is the first install and producing the actual .exe.

C) The installer .exe still doesn't exist. Without GitHub token, I can't trigger CI. Alternatives to get the exe built:
   - Ask again for token (user seems to want less friction).
   - Build in this sandbox? Linux, no MSVC. Cross-compiling JUCE with mingw is theoretically possible but practically unrealistic here (huge, plugins, Inno Setup needs wine, driver signing...). Not feasible within sandbox constraints/timeouts.

So what can I actually DO now to maximize automation without credentials?

Honest position: I need the GitHub token (2 min) — that's the one human step I can't do. The user hasn't given it. I should re-request it, but the user seems to have skipped it. Maybe they didn't understand. I should explain super simply and re-request.

But also, is there something I can automate now? I could:
1. Improve the phone-side app so it hosts the installer download URL directly (already does — user pastes URL in Settings).
2. Actually, wait — could the CI be replaced by something else? What about building the installer on-demand... no.

Alternatively — think differently about "automate everything": maybe I can reduce the whole thing to: user gives me the GitHub token ONCE; after that:
- Every time they ask me to update, I push code → CI builds → release published → user pastes release URL in phone app → phone serves to PC → PC auto-installs. That's already the design.

The user message "Solo con conectar el móvil por USB o la opción que me digas instale todo" = they want the end state: connect phone → everything installs. That's the designed flow but requires the one-time first installer + the token to build it.

So my response must:
1. Be honest: two things can't be automated away: (a) creating the GitHub key/token (I need it to publish the installer), (b) running the installer once on the PC the first time (Windows permission dialog). After that: yes, fully automatic.
2. Re-request the credentials via requestEnvs, with clearer, simpler instructions.

Should I do any code work now? Maybe I could simplify the phone flow: add a default/fallback URL field, or a "share link" helper. Actually one automation improvement: the Android app could let the user paste the GitHub release URL and it fetches the asset automatically. GitHub releases have predictable API: https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/latest → asset download URL. The PhoneSyncManager extracts version from URL filename — release asset will be named AcousticalEstudioSetup-1.0.0.exe (per workflow files: OutputBaseFilename=AcousticalEstudioSetup — wait, the .iss sets OutputBaseFilename=AcousticalEstudioSetup without version! The release upload uses the .exe as-is, named AcousticalEstudioSetup.exe. The Android regex needs version in URL. Hmm — the summary said user must paste URL containing version like Setup-1.1.0.exe. The CI names it without version. I should fix: either set OutputBaseFilename=AcousticalEstudioSetup-{#AppVersion} in the .iss, or have phone resolve the GitHub "latest release" API. 

Good improvement I can do NOW without credentials:
1. Fix .iss: OutputBaseFilename=AcousticalEstudioSetup-{#AppVersion} so the version appears in the filename (phone extracts version from URL).
2. Even better automation in the phone app: allow pasting the GitHub repo (owner/repo) instead of a full installer URL, and the app resolves the latest release automatically via the GitHub API. That makes "automate everything" real: after CI publishes a release, the user only pastes the repo name once, then just taps "Descargar" or even auto-checks.

That's a meaningful step toward automation I can implement now. But careful about scope creep — modifying PhoneSyncManager to fetch GitHub latest release. It already downloads from a URL; adding: if URL is a GitHub repo URL or owner/repo, resolve via api.github.com/repos/{repo}/releases/latest, find asset ending .exe. Reasonable size change.

Also need the token still — without it nothing gets published. Re-request via requestEnvs (force not needed; they weren't set).

Plan for this turn:
1. Edit installer .iss: versioned output filename.
2. Enhance PhoneSyncManager: GitHub "latest release" auto-resolution (if the user pastes a repo like github.com/user/repo or "user/repo", query the API, pick the .exe asset). Read the file first.
3. Update SettingsScreen text accordingly (mention "or paste your GitHub repository"). Need to read the WindowsPcCard section.
4. runChecks android.
5. Reply: explain what remains human (token once, first installer run once with UAC), re-request token via requestEnvs.

Let me read PhoneSyncManager.kt and the SettingsScreen section first.

Entendido — voy a dejar el proceso lo más automático posible. Primero reviso el código actual del servidor del móvil para añadir la pieza que falta: que el móvil resuelva solo el instalador más reciente de tu repositorio de GitHub (sin pegar enlaces largos cada vez).

The user says: "Please automate the whole process. Just by connecting the phone via USB or the option you tell me, install everything."

They didn't provide the GitHub token. Without it I can't publish the installer. But I can maximize automation on the phone side: make the phone app auto-resolve the latest release from GitHub so the user only pastes their repo once (or even after I set it as a default once known). Also fix the installer filename to include the version so the phone can extract it.
